lines.say: He poured forty gallons of bright white paint onto his roof...
while every single neighbor in the valley coated theirs in thick black tar.
Down here, summers hit a hundred and fifteen degrees,
and everyone swears dark tar is the only thing that seals out cracks.
You're blinding the whole street—and that chalk will wash off by July!
and the hottest heatwave in fifty years parks right over the town.
Inside the black-tar houses, the roofs act like giant frying pans—
soaking up the sun and baking the rooms underneath even at midnight.
Meanwhile, his white roof acts like a mirror,
bouncing almost ninety percent of that sunlight straight back into space before it ever turns into heat.
While every AC unit on the block trips the power grid,
he's sitting inside twenty degrees cooler—
without turning on a single machine.
